subject: Running gpagen on a landmarking set that used coords.subset?

messages.author: b7c0696a31d012d1
messages.subject: Running gpagen on a landmarking set that used coords.subset?
parts:
Hello everyone,

I have a set of 2D landmarks on the dorsal cranium of individual voles from nine different populations. Since there were missing landmarks in this dataset, I used the coords.subset function to subset the whole dataset by population (so within the whole dataset, there are now nine sub-arrays). I did this since I wanted the missing landmarks to be estimated based solely on the shape of the population the individual belongs to (rather than from the shapes of individuals across all the populations combined).

To estimate the locations of these missing landmarks, I first used the fixLMmirror function from package Morpho to estimate the bilateral landmarks (since I landmarked both sides of the cranium), then used the TPS method in geomorph's estimate.missing function to fill in any remaining missing landmarks. Once completing both of those steps, I checked to make sure that no missing landmarks remained (and none were found).

Next, I needed to run a generalized Procrustes analysis before I could analyze any of the size and shape data contained in my landmarking set. But this is where I ran into a problem. When I applied the coords.subset function to my whole dataset, that converted the 3D array my dataset started as into a list of nine 3D sub-arrays (representing each population), so gpagen sent an error message telling me that "Coordinates must be a 3D array". 

Is there a way to get gpagen to ignore the "list" aspect of my dataset so it can run the generalized Procrustes analysis on all the landmark coordinates within that list? Or is there a way to reconvert the list of my population arrays back into a single, ungrouped array without sacrificing the estimated landmarks I filled in? Any advice or suggestions would be greatly appreciated!!

Thanks,

Mariah

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Running gpagen on a landmarking set that used coords.subset?
parts:
Mariah,

If each list object is the same in dimension, simplfy2array will coerce a list into an array.

Mike
